image_description: A close-up, eye-level shot of an African crocodile (Nile crocodile) resting on a sandy riverbank. The head and upper torso are visible, showcasing the textured, armored skin with dark grey and brown scutes. The mouth is closed, revealing interlocking teeth along the jawline. The eye is prominent with a vertical slit pupil. The background consists of blurred water and sand.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers to a distinct point (V-shape), distinguishing it from the U-shape of an alligator. The head structure is broad and triangular as described.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The jawline clearly shows large, conical teeth protruding and interlocking even while the mouth is shut, a key characteristic of crocodiles.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is located on the top ridge of the skull (dorsal). The pupil is a clear vertical slit. While the nictitating membrane isn't actively covering the eye, the anatomical placement is correct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The nostrils are clearly visible at the very end of the snout, consistent with the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body behind the head shows thick, rugged armor plating typical of an elongated crocodilian form.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture displays distinct, raised bony plates (scutes) that appear to follow longitudinal alignment along the back.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of dark grey and muddy brown, and the texture is visibly rough and granular.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The crocodile is lying on its belly on the sand; the ventral (underbelly) surface is completely occluded by the ground and the angle of the shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The limbs are tucked under the body or out of frame; no feet or digits are visible for verification.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail extends out of the frame to the right; its full length and compression cannot be verified.

alignment_reasoning: All testable checkpoints regarding the head, face, and visible dorsal armor are perfectly met. The V-shaped snout, interlocking teeth, and specific scute texture align precisely with the Nile crocodile taxonomy. Non-testable checkpoints (ventral scales, limbs, tail) are occluded but do not contradict the visible evidence.
artifact_reasoning: No AI-generation artifacts detected. The image exhibits natural photographic depth of field, realistic skin micro-texture, and consistent lighting. Edges between the subject and the sandy foreground are sharp and physically plausible.

metadata.class_label: African crocodile, Nile crocodile, Crocodylus niloticus
